## Professional Summary

Quantitative social scientist using national linked administrative data to evaluate social policy and children's services, and to study inequalities in children's and young people's mental health and access to care. Combines quasi-experimental and multilevel methods with qualitative work, evidence reviews and co-production with young people and parents. Research lead on a Department for Education commissioned evaluation that contributed evidence to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026.

---

## Research Appointments

**Research Fellow** | UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health, Population, Policy and Practice | November 2025 to present

*NIHR Children and Families Policy Research Unit; Population Health Improvement UK (PHI-UK)*

- Research lead for the challenge area on children and young people's mental health in the Population Mental Health Consortium (PHI-UK)
- Designing and leading a two-paper programme applying intersectional MAIHDA to referrals to NHS mental health services in England, using the National Pupil Database linked to the Mental Health Services Data Set
- Co-designing workshops with young people, facilitated by Leaders Unlocked, on inequalities in access to mental health services
- Contributed ECHILD analyses to the research for the Independent Review into Mental Health Conditions, ADHD and Autism (final report October 2026)
- Led the post-peer-review revision of a national ECHILD cohort study of 5.6 million pupils (*BMJ Public Health*, in press)
- Maintain the ECHILD study website (R, GitHub) and contribute to the ECHILD User Guide and data catalogue

**Research Assistant (part-time)** | UCL Division of Psychiatry and Centre for Longitudinal Studies | September 2025 to 2026

*UCL Grand Challenges*

- Conducted the quantitative analysis for a quasi-experimental evaluation of statutory Relationships and Sex Education and mental health inequality between sexual minority and heterosexual adolescents, using the UK Household Longitudinal Study under special licence
- Wrote the statistical analysis plan: difference-in-differences with event-study pre-trend tests, and a Bayesian interrupted time series in R-INLA
- Co-led a public involvement session with LGBTQ+ young people
- Joint first author of the resulting paper (in preparation)

**Research Lead, Evaluation of Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hubs** | Thomas Coram Research Unit, UCL Social Research Institute | February 2024 to September 2025

*Commissioned by the Department for Education through Foundations, the What Works Centre for Children and Families (£200,000)*

- Co-wrote the funding application and led its submission
- Led a mixed-methods implementation and process evaluation, combining national survey analysis with case studies in three local authorities (about 40 interviews)
- Ran public involvement work with parents with experience of children's social care
- Presented quarterly to a cross-government steering committee (NHS England, DfE, DHSC, Home Office), led two DfE workshops and briefed the National Police Chiefs' Council
- First author of the evaluation report (Foundations, 2025), which contributed evidence to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 and was cited in the Sara Sharif Child Safeguarding Practice Review

**Research Assistant (part-time)** | UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health | August 2022 to February 2023

*Child Development Assessment Project, commissioned by the Department of Health and Social Care*

- Led a rapid systematic review of child development assessment tools, from protocol to final report
- Co-authored the commissioned report (2023) and two journal articles (*BMJ Open*, 2024; *Journal of Public Health*, 2026)

**Research Assistant** | UCL Institute of Education | March to September 2021

- Regression analysis of educational outcomes for refugee children using Ugandan survey data

**Research Assistant** | International Inequalities Institute, LSE | September 2019 to September 2021

- Harmonised longitudinal survey data from nine countries for comparative research on job quality
- Co-authored three peer-reviewed articles (*World Development*, *Social Indicators Research*, *Regional Studies*)

**Researcher and Project Manager** | Centre for Conflict Studies and Social Cohesion, Universidad de Chile | November 2016 to April 2019

- Microeconometric analysis of employment quality in Latin America and the EU; financial administration and reporting for the projects

**Junior Researcher** | FUSADES, El Salvador | June 2012 to April 2015

- Analysis of household surveys, firm-level data and health administrative data on poverty, competitiveness, education and health spending

## Technical Skills

**Software**: R (5+ years, teaching level), Stata (11+ years, teaching level), Quarto, GitHub, REDCap, NVivo, QGIS/ArcGIS, SQL (basic), Python (developing)

**Quantitative Methods**: Difference-in-differences (including staggered adoption), synthetic controls, interrupted time series, survival and person-time models, multilevel modelling and intersectional MAIHDA, Bayesian modelling in R-INLA, survey design, web scraping and text mining

**Qualitative and Review Methods**: Semi-structured interviews, focus groups, thematic and framework analysis, systematic and scoping reviews, public involvement and co-production

**Data Access**: ONS Approved Researcher (since 2021), ONS Secure Research Service, UK Data Service special licence, UCL Data Safe Haven

**Selected Training**: Bayesian Statistics, UCL (2026); evaluation methods with administrative data, ADR UK (2026); Cambridge Econometrics Summer School (2025); CEMMAP Policy Evaluation Methods (2023); Survival Analysis, Scottish Longitudinal Study (2023)

**Languages**: English and Spanish (native fluency); Italian (basic)
